entities.summary:
Ad van Luyn (Adrianus Herman van Luyn, b. 1935) is a Dutch Salesian bishop who served as Bishop of Rotterdam in the Netherlands from 1993 to 2011. Born in the Netherlands and ordained as a Salesian priest, he pursued a career combining religious order work with episcopal leadership in one of Western Europe's most secular societies.

Rotterdam's diocese encompasses Europe's largest port city and one of the most demographically diverse metropolitan areas in the Netherlands. Its Catholic community includes both Dutch-heritage Catholics and large communities of migrants from Catholic countries — Portugal, Poland, Cape Verde, Morocco — creating a multiculturally diverse pastoral context unusual even by European standards. Van Luyn's episcopal ministry navigated this extraordinary diversity while addressing the severe decline of traditional Dutch Catholicism.

As a Salesian bishop, he brought Don Bosco's charism of youth ministry and practical Christianity to a diocese facing acute secularisation. He was also an active voice in the European Church, serving on committees of the Council of European Bishops' Conferences (CCEE) and engaging with the question of Europe's Christian heritage and its secular future. He was a careful, low-profile bishop who avoided the polarising controversies that had marked earlier Dutch Catholic leadership.
